title: Agentic Engineering
subtitle: From Autonomous Agents to Governed Capabilities
promise: Engineer useful autonomous work that stays within authority and leaves evidence you can defend.
audience: Engineers, architects, operators and technical leaders designing agentic systems.

sourceBrief.path: docs/Agentic Engineering - From Autonomous Agents to Governed Capabilities.md

concepts.title: Intent
concepts.question: What human result is worth producing?
concepts.meaning: State the purpose, the beneficiary and the exclusions before selecting an agent or tool.
concepts.example: She wants an inspection report. Publication is excluded.
concepts.failure: A broad goal is mistaken for permission to perform every useful action.

concepts.title: Scenario
concepts.question: What changes for the human?
concepts.meaning: Describe Input, Event and Outcome as observable conditions. Data becomes action; action changes an experience.
concepts.example: Input: a candidate awaits inspection. Event: inspect within scope. Outcome: a useful report; publication remains pending.
concepts.failure: A list of technical tasks never establishes what success means.

concepts.title: Authority
concepts.question: Who may authorize the effect?
concepts.meaning: Bind the exact request to its permitted boundary and the person or authority that can change it.
concepts.example: Inspection authority cannot silently expand into publication authority.
concepts.failure: Access to a tool is treated as authorization to use it.

concepts.title: Agent responsibility
concepts.question: What is the agent actually accountable for?
concepts.meaning: Give the agent a bounded responsibility, explicit outputs and a legal continuation when a request cannot proceed.
concepts.example: The agent can propose an inspection. It cannot grant itself publication permission.
concepts.failure: The same agent supplies both the proposal and its approval.

concepts.title: Capability & provider
concepts.question: What meaning must survive a provider change?
concepts.meaning: Keep the expected input, effect, output and proof obligations stable. Require a compatible realizer for that responsibility.
concepts.example: Either inspection adapter must return the same inspection product under the same authority.
concepts.failure: Changing the model quietly changes the job, its scope or its acceptance criteria.

concepts.title: Execution
concepts.question: What crosses into the world?
concepts.meaning: Distinguish a decision from the effect it permits. Admit only the exact mechanic at the covered boundary.
concepts.example: An ALLOW label is a decision. It does not establish an intercepted or completed tool action.
concepts.failure: A returned status is presented as evidence that a live effect was controlled.

concepts.title: Testimony
concepts.question: Can the result be traced to this request?
concepts.meaning: Retain attributable artifacts that connect request, authority, decision, provider and actual effect. Check what each artifact really supports.
concepts.example: A probe receipt must identify the session and observed effect. A diagram supplies no such receipt.
concepts.failure: Logs or model confidence are promoted into proof without a scoped claim.

concepts.title: Evaluation
concepts.question: Does the evidence close the promised claim?
concepts.meaning: Compare the exact evidence with the outcome and failure obligations. Keep missing evidence separate from contradictory evidence.
concepts.example: Both deny and permit probes must close in the same identity envelope. One successful probe is insufficient.
concepts.failure: A green happy path conceals an uncovered path or stale evidence.

concepts.title: Governed outcome
concepts.question: Did useful work finish with authority intact?
concepts.meaning: Close the human scenario only to the extent supported by evidence. Preserve the next decision for the authority that owns it.
concepts.example: The engineer receives her report and still controls publication.
concepts.failure: Task completion is claimed while authority or evidence has been lost.

modules.defense: Show why the requested publication stays pending, then specify the proof that would permit inspection.
Show which source statement supports every visual claim, and where a reviewer can challenge it.
Identify the exact failed output that must hold a dependent stage.
Show the obligations that stay invariant when the provider changes.
Distinguish restoring artifacts from proving their exact preservation.
Explain which representation serves the review and why possession grants no authority.
Show the conformance finding that decides the round and the smallest legal repair.
Show why the exact shared baseline changes what can be claimed as published.
Classify an absent artifact separately from an integrity mismatch.
Show what the response proves and what still needs a separate admission decision.

pathways.title: Agentic Engineering Foundations
pathways.outcome: Frame autonomy through scenarios, authority, effects and evidence.

pathways.title: Agentic Engineering Practitioner
pathways.outcome: Implement bounded tools, state, memory, orchestration and evaluation.

pathways.outcome: Present a governed capability and defend its architecture, evidence and unresolved gaps.

providers.label: Inspection adapter A
providers.explanation: Illustrative adapter: fulfills the inspection contract.

providers.label: Inspection adapter B
providers.explanation: Alternate illustrative adapter: the same input, output and authority obligations.

providers.label: Narration-only adapter
providers.explanation: It can produce audio, but cannot supply the inspection product.

providers.label: Unavailable inspection adapter
providers.explanation: It declares the right responsibility but is unavailable in this exercise.

briefFields.label: Human intent and scenario
briefFields.prompt: Who benefits? Describe the input, event and observable outcome.

briefFields.label: Authority and excluded effects
briefFields.prompt: Who owns the decision? What can this agent do, and what remains out of scope?

briefFields.label: Provider obligations
briefFields.prompt: Which input, output, effect and evidence obligations must survive provider substitution?

briefFields.label: Execution testimony
briefFields.prompt: What artifacts connect the exact request, authority, decision and actual effect?

briefFields.label: Failure and evaluation plan
briefFields.prompt: What would disprove success? Cover denial, permission, identity drift and missing evidence.

briefFields.label: Engineering closure
briefFields.prompt: Separate what exists, the intended experience, and the next mechanic or proof needed.

rubric.criterion: The human outcome and exclusions are explicit.
rubric.defense: Name an action that is useful but still unauthorized.

rubric.criterion: Authority and agent responsibility remain separate.
rubric.defense: Explain why access, confidence or a prior success cannot expand authority.

rubric.criterion: Provider substitution preserves the capability contract.
rubric.defense: Demonstrate one compatible replacement and one incompatible candidate.

rubric.criterion: Each completion claim has scoped evidence and a failure test.
rubric.defense: Show the exact missing receipt or contradictory finding that prevents closure.
